barcode.title: Barcode Generator
barcode.intro: Online barcode generator supporting CODE128, EAN-13, EAN-8, UPC-A, CODE39, ITF-14 and more formats, with customizable size and text display
barcode.infoIntro: Barcode Generation: From Numbers to Scannable Visual Encoding
barcode.problem1: The 'beep' at checkout counters, the black stripes on express labels, the numeric patterns on book covers — these are all barcodes, but they follow completely different encoding standards. CODE128 can encode any ASCII character, EAN-13 can only encode 13 digits but is globally universal, UPC-A is the North American product standard, and CODE39 is used in industrial and military fields — choose the wrong encoding format and the scanner won't read it.
barcode.problem2: This tool supports 8 barcode standards: CODE128 (general), EAN-13 (products), EAN-8 (small products), UPC-A (US), CODE39 (industrial), ITF-14 (logistics cartons), MSI (inventory), Pharmacode (pharmaceuticals). Each format has strict character set and digit limits — the tool automatically validates input against the selected format's requirements, preventing generation of unreadable 'waste codes'.
barcode.problem3: Based on the JsBarcode library, barcodes are generated as vector graphics in the browser — output in SVG format, so they never blur no matter how much you zoom in. You can customize width, height, and whether to show text. Generated barcodes can be downloaded as SVG files or printed directly on labels.
barcode.formatTitle: 2. Applicable Scenarios for Eight Encoding Standards
barcode.formatCode128: CODE128: The most universal barcode format — can encode all 128 ASCII characters (digits, letters, symbols). High density, large capacity, widely used for logistics packages, asset management, and internal numbering. No digit limit; theoretically can encode strings of any length.
barcode.formatEan13: EAN-13: The 'ID card' for global retail products — 13 digits, with the first 2-3 being the country code (China's is 690-699), followed by manufacturer code, product code, and a check digit. If you need a barcode for retail products that can be scanned at supermarkets, choose EAN-13.
barcode.formatUpc: UPC-A: North American product standard — 12 digits, essentially EAN-13 without the country code (US country code is implicitly 0). If your products are mainly sold in the North American market, choose UPC-A.
barcode.featureOnline: SVG Vector Output: Barcodes are rendered in SVG — every line is a vector path, not pixels. This means edges stay sharp and clear no matter how much you zoom in. Print on labels, embed in documents, display on web pages — never blurry.
barcode.featurePreview: Real-time Preview: Barcodes generate and display instantly after entering content. Updates in real time when switching formats or adjusting width/height — no need to click a 'Generate' button.
barcode.featureExport: Customizable Size: Width (thickness of each line, 1-5px) and height (overall barcode height, 20-200px) are both adjustable. Too small a width may prevent scanners from recognizing the barcode — 2px minimum is recommended.
barcode.featureSecurity: Show/Hide Text: The text below the barcode (human-readable characters) can be shown or hidden. Show text for manual verification on printed labels; hide it for machine-only scanning scenarios.
barcode.usageInput1: Enter encoded content: Enter corresponding content based on the selected format — CODE128 accepts any text, EAN-13 requires 13 digits, UPC-A requires 12 digits.
barcode.usageInput2: Format validation: The tool checks in real time whether input meets format requirements. Shows red error messages when it doesn't — e.g., entering letters in EAN-13 will prompt 'digits only'.
barcode.usageInput3: Check digit: The last digit of EAN-13/UPC-A is a check digit — if you enter one digit short, the tool automatically calculates and fills in the check digit.
barcode.usageFormat1: CODE128: General format, supports any ASCII character. Suitable for internal numbering, asset management.
barcode.usageFormat2: EAN-13: Product standard, 13 digits. Suitable for retail products.
barcode.usageFormat3: EAN-8: Small product standard, 8 digits. Suitable for small packaging (not enough space for EAN-13).
barcode.usageFormat4: UPC-A: North American product standard, 12 digits. Suitable for the North American market.
barcode.usageFormat5: CODE39: Industrial standard, supports digits and uppercase letters. Suitable for manufacturing, military.
barcode.usageFormat6: ITF-14: Logistics carton standard, 14 digits. Suitable for outer carton labeling.
barcode.usageStyle1: Width: Thickness of each line (1-5px). For printing, 2-3px is recommended; for screen display, 1-2px works.
barcode.usageStyle2: Height: Overall barcode height (20-200px). Recommend at least 50px — barcodes that are too short may be hard for scanners to recognize.
barcode.usageStyle3: Show text: Whether to display encoded content below the barcode. Recommended for printed labels; can be hidden for web embedding.
barcode.usageGenerate1: SVG Download: Click the download button to save an SVG file. SVG is a vector format that can be scaled without quality loss.
barcode.usageGenerate2: For Printing: SVG files can be directly imported into design software like AI/CDR for layout and printing. You can also print directly from the browser.
barcode.usageGenerate3: PNG Needs: If the target system doesn't support SVG, you can export to PNG from design software — resolution of 300dpi or higher is recommended.
barcode.usageAdvice1: Contrast: Barcodes must have high contrast — black bars on white background is the safest combination. Avoid colored barcodes (many scanners can't read red barcodes).
barcode.usageAdvice2: Quiet Zone: Leave 'quiet zones' on both sides of the barcode (at least 5mm of blank space) — scanners rely on quiet zones to identify the start and end of the barcode.
barcode.usageAdvice3: Minimum Size: The standard size for EAN-13 is 37.29mm x 25.93mm, which can be scaled down to 80% (about 30mm wide). Below 80% may affect scan success rate.
barcode.usageAdvice4: Print Quality: Ensure the barcode area has no creases, stains, or ink spread — these all cause scanning failures. Thermal transfer or laser printing is recommended.
barcode.noteSecurity1: Pure Front-end Generation: Barcodes are generated entirely in the browser — never uploaded to any server. Your encoded content stays local.
barcode.noteSecurity2: No Dependencies: No software or font installation needed. The JsBarcode library is embedded in the page.
barcode.noteSecurity3: Offline Available: After the page loads, barcodes can be generated normally even without internet.
barcode.noteFormat1: Not sure which to choose? For retail products choose EAN-13, for internal management choose CODE128, for the North American market choose UPC-A, for logistics cartons choose ITF-14.
barcode.noteFormat2: EAN-13 Check Digit: The last digit is a Modulo 10 check digit — the tool calculates it automatically, you only need to enter the first 12 digits (or all 13 including the check digit).
barcode.noteFormat3: CODE128 Character Set: Supports all ASCII characters (0-127), including uppercase/lowercase letters, digits, punctuation and spaces.
barcode.noteFormat4: ITF-14 Features: Can only encode 14 digits, specifically for logistics carton identification. Uses a different encoding algorithm than EAN-13.
barcode.noteCheck1: EAN and UPC formats require a correct check digit.
barcode.noteCheck2: An incorrect check digit will make the barcode unscannable.
barcode.noteCheck3: It is recommended to use standard check digit generation tools for calculation.
barcode.notePrint1: Barcodes need sufficient contrast — black bars on white background is the safest combination. Avoid red barcodes (many scanners use red light, so red bars become 'invisible') or dark barcodes on colored backgrounds.
barcode.notePrint2: Barcode size cannot be arbitrarily scaled — the width of each barcode module must not be less than 0.19mm (7.5 mil), otherwise scanners may not be able to read it. High-resolution PNG downloads ensure sufficient module width at 300 DPI printing.
barcode.notePrint3: A 'quiet zone' (blank area) is needed around the barcode — at least 10 module widths. If the quiet zone is insufficient, scanners may not correctly identify the barcode boundary. Images generated by this tool already include appropriate quiet zones.
barcode.noteFaq1: Q: Scanner can't read the generated barcode? A: Check: 1) Is the format correct (EAN-13 content must be 13 digits); 2) Is the width too small (recommend ≥2px); 3) Is the print clear (no blur/broken lines).
barcode.noteFaq2: Q: Can I generate colored barcodes? A: Technically yes, but strongly discouraged. Most scanners use red LEDs — red barcodes are nearly invisible under red light, the scanner will think 'there's no barcode'.
barcode.noteFaq3: Q: Can I generate multiple barcodes at once? A: The current version generates one at a time. For batch generation, you can modify the input content and generate/download one by one.
barcode.errorPharmacodeRange: Pharmacode must be a number between 3 and 131070
barcode.formatHintCode128: CODE128 supports digits, letters and special characters
barcode.formatHintCode39: CODE39 supports letters, digits and special symbols
barcode.formatHintMsi: MSI supports digits of any length
barcode.formatHintPharmacode: Pharmacode must be a number between 3 and 131070
barcode.usageSelectFormat: Select encoding standard: Choose the barcode format from the dropdown. For retail products choose EAN-13 or UPC-A; for logistics packages choose ITF-14; for general use choose CODE128; for industrial manufacturing choose CODE39. Different formats have different input requirements — EAN/UPC only allow digits, CODE128 supports any character.
barcode.usageInputContent: Enter encoded data: Type the barcode content in the input box. EAN-13 requires 12-13 digits (if you enter 12, the system auto-calculates the 13th check digit); UPC-A requires 12 digits; CODE128 supports ASCII strings of any length. An error message appears if input doesn't meet format requirements.
barcode.usageWidth: Adjust bar width: Use the 'Width' option to adjust the width of each barcode module — thin (1px), normal (2px), wide (3px). Wider bars are better for long-distance scanning and large-format printing; narrower bars suit small labels and high-density encoding.
barcode.usageHeight: Adjust height: Use the 'Height' option to adjust the overall barcode height — short (50px), normal (80px), tall (120px), extra tall (150px). Barcode height affects the scanner's reading distance — the taller the barcode, the farther the scanning distance. Retail products typically use 80px height.
barcode.usageShowValue: Show/hide text: Use the 'Show Value' toggle to control whether encoded content text is displayed below the barcode. For print use, typically enable display (for manual verification); when embedding in system interfaces, typically hide it.
barcode.usageDownload: Download PNG: Once satisfied with the barcode result, click the 'Download PNG' button to save the barcode as a high-resolution PNG image. The image can be used directly for printing, embedding in documents, or sending to suppliers.

color-picker.title: Color Picker
color-picker.intro: Color picker supporting HEX, RGB, HSL color format conversion, real-time visual color picking preview, common color presets and one-click copy
color-picker.infoIntro: Color Picker: From Color Wheel to Code — Precise Color Conversion
color-picker.problem1: Designers use HSL in Photoshop, front-end engineers write HEX in CSS, Python scripts need RGB tuples, Java's Color class needs 0-255 integers — the same color has completely different representations across tools and languages. Manual conversion is not only tedious but error-prone — what's #3B82F6 in RGB? Most people can't calculate it correctly.
color-picker.problem2: This tool provides comprehensive color selection and conversion: visual color wheel picking, real-time conversion among HEX/RGB/HSL/HSV/CMYK formats, CSS gradient generator, and palette extraction. Click anywhere on the color wheel and all five format values update simultaneously — no manual input or calculation needed.
color-picker.problem3: Supports reverse color selection from HEX values — enter a color code and the color wheel auto-positions to the corresponding spot. Also supports random harmonious color scheme generation (complementary, triadic, tetradic, analogous) — helping designers quickly find coordinated color palettes.
color-picker.formatTitle: 2. Technical Background of Five Color Formats
color-picker.formatHex: HEX (#RRGGBB): The standard format for CSS and web design. 6 hexadecimal digits, every two representing a color channel (red/green/blue), range #000000 to #FFFFFF. Can represent 16.7 million colors. Concise and intuitive, the first choice for front-end development.
color-picker.formatEan13: RGB (rgb(r, g, b)): Additive color model — red, green, blue primary light叠加. Each channel 0-255 integer value. Used for Canvas API, image processing, screen display. RGB(255, 0, 0) = pure red, RGB(0, 0, 0) = black.
color-picker.formatHsl: HSL (hsl(h, s%, l%)): The most intuitive color model for humans — hue (0-360° color wheel angle), saturation (0%-100% vividness), lightness (0%-100% brightness). 'Make this red a bit lighter' in HSL just means increasing the L value.
color-picker.formatRgb: RGB (rgb(r, g, b)): Additive color model — red, green, and blue primary light combined. Each channel ranges from 0-255 as integer values. Used in Canvas API, image processing, and screen display. RGB(255, 0, 0) = pure red, RGB(0, 0, 0) = black.
color-picker.featureOnline: Visual Color Wheel: Click or drag on the HSL color wheel to pick colors — the outer ring is hue (H), the inner area is a 2D plane of saturation (S) and lightness (L). More intuitive than typing numbers — click where you see the color you want.
color-picker.featurePreview: Five-Color Sync: After selecting any color, HEX, RGB, HSL, HSV, CMYK formats all display simultaneously with one-click copy. Modify any format's value and the others auto-sync.
color-picker.featureExport: CSS Gradient Generator: Select two or more colors to auto-generate linear-gradient or radial-gradient CSS code. Real-time gradient preview with adjustable angle and color stops.
color-picker.featureSecurity: Harmonious Color Schemes: Auto-generates color schemes based on color wheel angle relationships — complementary (180° opposite), triadic (120° equal division), tetradic (90° equal division), analogous (±30° neighbors). Helps quickly find coordinated color combinations.
color-picker.featurePicker: Screen Color Picker: Based on the HTML5 EyeDropper API (Chrome/Edge support) or Canvas pixel sampling. Click the pick button, the cursor becomes a crosshair, click anywhere on the page to capture the precise color value at that point. For browsers without EyeDropper API support, an image upload color picking alternative is provided.
color-picker.usagePick1: Click the color swatch: Click the color preview block on the left to open the system color picker.
color-picker.usagePick2: Drag to select: Drag in the color picker to choose the desired color.
color-picker.usagePick3: Preset colors: Click a common color below to select it quickly.
color-picker.usageHex1: Hexadecimal: Starts with # and consists of 6 hexadecimal digits (0-9, A-F).
color-picker.usageHex2: Input: Enter a 6-digit color value directly; it is automatically converted to uppercase.
color-picker.usageHex3: Shorthand support: 3-digit shorthand (e.g., #FFF) is supported and automatically expanded to 6 digits.
color-picker.usageHex4: Copy: Click the 'Copy' button to copy the full HEX value.
color-picker.usageRgb1: Red/Green/Blue: Consists of red, green and blue components, each ranging from 0-255.
color-picker.usageRgb2: R value: Red component; 0 means no red, 255 means maximum red.
color-picker.usageRgb3: G value: Green component; 0 means no green, 255 means maximum green.
color-picker.usageRgb4: B value: Blue component; 0 means no blue, 255 means maximum blue.
color-picker.usageRgb5: Copy: Click the 'Copy' button to copy the rgb(r, g, b) format.
color-picker.usageHsl1: H Hue: The type of color, ranging 0-360 degrees (red 0°, green 120°, blue 240°).
color-picker.usageHsl2: S Saturation: The purity of the color, 0%-100% (0% is gray, 100% is pure).
color-picker.usageHsl3: L Lightness: The brightness of the color, 0%-100% (0% is black, 50% is normal, 100% is white).
color-picker.usageHsl4: Copy: Click the 'Copy' button to copy the hsl(h, s%, l%) format.
color-picker.usageConvert1: Real-time conversion: Modifying any format's value automatically syncs the other formats.
color-picker.usageConvert2: Mutual conversion: The three formats are fully equivalent and can be converted freely.
color-picker.usageConvert3: Copy all: Click the 'Copy All Formats' button to copy all three formats at once.
color-picker.usageAdvice1: 60-30-10 Rule: Primary color 60% (background), secondary color 30% (content area), accent color 10% (buttons/links). This is the most classic proportion.
color-picker.usageAdvice2: Contrast Check: Text-to-background contrast ratio should be at least 4.5:1 (WCAG AA standard) — ensure readability. White text on light gray backgrounds is a common readability disaster.
color-picker.usageAdvice3: Color Blind Friendly: Avoid relying solely on red-green differences to convey information — red-green color blindness is the most common color vision deficiency (affecting ~8% of males). Use shapes/text as auxiliary distinction.
color-picker.usageAdvice4: Dark Mode Adaptation: When designing dark themes, don't simply invert lightness — you need to readjust saturation. High saturation colors on dark backgrounds create a 'glowing' effect that causes visual fatigue.
color-picker.noteSecurity1: Pure Front-end Tool: All color calculations are done in the browser — never uploaded to any server.
color-picker.noteSecurity2: No Network Dependency: Works offline after the page loads.
color-picker.noteSecurity3: No Data Storage: Does not save your color selection history — every open is a fresh start.
color-picker.noteFormat1: HEX and RGB: Direct correspondence — every two digits of HEX is the hexadecimal value of one RGB channel. #FF0000 = RGB(255, 0, 0).
color-picker.noteFormat2: RGB and HSL: Requires mathematical conversion — HSL hue is determined by the difference between the max and min RGB channel values, saturation and lightness by their sum.
color-picker.noteFormat3: RGB and CMYK: CMYK is a subtractive model (ink absorbs light), RGB is an additive model (screen emits light). They can't perfectly correspond — some vivid RGB colors cannot be precisely reproduced in CMYK.
color-picker.noteFormat4: Color Gamut Limitation: Screens display in sRGB gamut, CMYK printing gamut is different — colors seen on screen may differ from actual print results. Important projects should be proofed first.
color-picker.noteInput2: Out-of-range values are automatically clamped to the valid range.
color-picker.noteInput3: Values are validated and converted in real time as you type.
color-picker.noteFaq1: Q: Color looks different on phone? A: Different devices have different screen gamuts and color calibration — the same color may vary between iPhone and Android. Design based on sRGB standard.
color-picker.noteFaq2: Q: Can I enter color names? A: Current version doesn't support CSS color names (like red, blue). Please enter HEX or RGB values directly.
color-picker.noteFaq3: Q: Gradient code doesn't work in old browsers? A: CSS gradients may need browser prefixes (-webkit-, -moz-). Modern browsers (post-2020) don't need prefixes.
color-picker.usagePickerClick: Click the pick button: After clicking the 'Pick' button, the cursor changes to a crosshair shape (requires EyeDropper API support). Click anywhere on the screen to get the precise color value at that point. The picking range is not limited to this tool page — you can pick colors from anywhere within the browser window.
color-picker.usagePickerResult: View color values: After picking, the color preview area immediately updates to the captured color, showing HEX, RGB, HSL format values simultaneously. Each value has a copy button for one-click clipboard copy.
color-picker.usageManualHSL: HSL color disk: Click on the HSL color disk to select hue and saturation, adjust lightness on the brightness bar. HSL mode best matches human intuition about color — hue (what color), saturation (vividness), lightness (brightness) are three independent dimensions.
color-picker.usageManualRGB: RGB sliders: Adjust each channel's intensity (0-255) with red, green, blue sliders. RGB mode is ideal for precise control of how colors display on screen — since monitors themselves emit light through RGB primary color mixing.
color-picker.usageManualInput: Direct color value input: Enter HEX (e.g. #EA580C), RGB (e.g. rgb(234,88,12)) or HSL (e.g. hsl(17,82%,48%)) format color values directly. The color disk and preview area auto-update to the corresponding color, and other format values sync-calculate.
color-picker.noteEyedropper1: Screen color picking depends on the EyeDropper API, currently only supported by Chrome and Edge (Chromium-based). Firefox and Safari don't support this API yet. In unsupported browsers, use the image upload color picking alternative.
color-picker.noteEyedropper2: The color picker can only capture colors within the browser window — it cannot pick colors from the desktop or other applications outside the browser. To pick colors from other apps, take a screenshot first and use the image upload feature.
color-picker.noteEyedropper3: Picking accuracy is affected by monitor gamut and browser color management. On wide-gamut (P3/DCI-P3) displays, picking results may differ slightly from sRGB standard values. Use HEX values for cross-device color alignment.
color-picker.usageInput1: Color wheel picking: Click on the HSL color wheel to select hue, then click in the square area to select saturation and lightness.
color-picker.usageInput2: HEX input: Enter a color code directly (e.g. #3B82F6), the color wheel auto-positions to the corresponding color.
color-picker.usageInput3: RGB input: Enter R/G/B values separately (0-255), the color wheel and HEX auto-update.
color-picker.usageFormat1: HEX: Click the copy button, paste directly into CSS code.
color-picker.usageFormat2: RGB: Click the copy button, format is rgb(r, g, b).
color-picker.usageFormat3: HSL: Click the copy button, format is hsl(h, s%, l%).
color-picker.usageFormat4: HSV: Hue-Saturation-Value model, similar to HSL but with different lightness calculation. Design software (like Photoshop) commonly uses this format.
color-picker.usageFormat5: CMYK: Print four-color — cyan, magenta, yellow, black. Used for print design to ensure screen-to-print color consistency.
color-picker.usageFormat6: One-click copy: Each format has a copy button, click to auto-copy to clipboard.
color-picker.usageStyle1: Complementary: Colors 180° apart on the color wheel — strongest contrast (e.g. red and green, blue and orange). Suitable for designs needing visual impact.
color-picker.usageStyle2: Triadic: Three colors 120° apart on the color wheel — balanced and rich. Suitable for lively, colorful designs.
color-picker.usageStyle3: Analogous: 2-5 adjacent colors on the color wheel — harmonious and unified. Suitable for minimalist, elegant designs.
color-picker.usageGenerate1: Select colors: Choose 2-5 colors as gradient stops.
color-picker.usageGenerate2: Adjust direction: Set gradient angle (0-360°) or choose radial gradient.
color-picker.usageGenerate3: Copy code: One-click copy CSS gradient code, paste directly into stylesheets.
color-picker.formatCode128: HEX (#RRGGBB): The standard format for CSS and web design. 6 hexadecimal digits, two per color channel (Red/Green/Blue), ranging from #000000 to #FFFFFF. Represents 16.77 million colors. Simple and intuitive — the go-to choice for front-end development.
color-picker.formatUpc: HSL (hsl(h, s%, l%)): The most intuitive color model — Hue (0-360° on the color wheel), Saturation (0%-100% vividness), Lightness (0%-100% brightness). "Make this red a bit brighter" in HSL just means increasing the L value.

diff.title: Text Comparison Tool
diff.intro: A text comparison tool that highlights added, removed and modified content when comparing two texts or files, with word-level diff support
diff.placeholderText: Enter or paste two texts above, then click "Compare" to view the differences
diff.infoIntro: Text Comparison: Find Differences Line by Line, Character by Character
diff.problemTitle: 1. Visual Comparison Is the Least Efficient Quality Control Method
diff.problem1: Where are the differences between two code files? What changed between contract V1 and V2? What discrepancies exist between the translation and the original? Which parameter was modified in the config file? These scenarios require precise text comparison — scanning line by line with the naked eye is not only slow but extremely error-prone. This tool is based on the classic Myers diff algorithm, precisely identifying added, removed, and modified content at the line level.
diff.problem2: Paste two texts into the left and right input boxes, click the 'Compare' button, and immediately see the differences — added content highlighted in green, removed content in red, modified content marked in yellow. Supports ignoring whitespace differences and case differences — adapting to different comparison needs.
diff.problem3: Pure front-end implementation — text comparison is done in the browser, nothing is uploaded to any server. Supports text comparison of any length (limited by browser memory, typically can handle tens of thousands of lines). Comparison results can be copied with one click or viewed directly.
diff.formatText: Line-Level Matching: The algorithm splits both texts by lines, then finds the longest common subsequence (LCS) — lines that appear in both texts in the same order with the same content. Lines not in the common sequence are marked as differences: lines unique to the left side are marked as "deleted," lines unique to the right side are marked as "added."
diff.formatCode: Myers Algorithm: This tool uses Eugene Myers' O(ND) diff algorithm — time complexity is proportional to the difference between the two texts, not the product of their lengths. This means even comparing two 10,000-line files is fast if only 50 lines differ.
diff.featureOnline: Side-by-side View: Left and right columns display the original and compared texts respectively — differing lines are highlighted with colors, aligned display for easy line-by-line comparison.
diff.featurePreview: Color Coding: Green = lines added on the right, Red = lines removed from the left, Yellow = modified lines (present on both sides but different content), Gray = unchanged context lines.
diff.featureExport: Statistics: After comparison, shows difference statistics — number of added lines, removed lines, modified lines, total differences. Quickly understand the extent of differences between two texts.
diff.featureSecurity: Pure Local Processing: Text comparison is done entirely in the browser — your code, contracts, configs and other sensitive content are never uploaded to any server.
diff.usageDirectInput: Direct input: Enter or paste content into the "Original Text" box on the left and the "New Text" box on the right.
diff.usageUpload: Upload a file: Click the "Open File" button to choose a local text file (supports .txt, .json, .xml, .html, .css, .js, .ts, .md, etc.).
diff.usageFileFormat: File format: Only plain text files are supported; binary files (images, PDFs, archives, etc.) are not.
diff.optionContext: Show identical lines: When checked, all lines are shown, including unchanged ones.
diff.optionWordDiff: Word-level diff: When checked, the specific changed words in each differing line are highlighted.
diff.optionSwap: Swap texts: Click the ⇄ button to swap the content of the left and right panels.
diff.viewCompare: Compare: Click the "Compare" button to run the text comparison.
diff.viewRealtime: Real-time compare: Comparison is triggered automatically when the text changes (500ms delay).
diff.viewAdd: Added lines: Green background, prefixed with "+", indicating lines added in the new text.
diff.viewDel: Removed lines: Red background, prefixed with "-", indicating lines removed from the original text.
diff.viewMod: Modified lines: Yellow background, indicating lines with differences.
diff.viewStats: Statistics: Shows the counts of added, removed and identical lines.
diff.tipClear: Clear text: Click the "Clear" button to remove all input content.
diff.tipCopy: Copy results: Select the text directly in the diff result to copy it.
diff.tipShortcut: Keyboard shortcut: Press Enter to trigger the comparison.
diff.scenarioCode: Code comparison: Compare differences between code versions.
diff.scenarioDoc: Document comparison: Check what changed in a document before and after editing.
diff.scenarioConfig: Config comparison: Compare differences between configuration files.
diff.scenarioLog: Log comparison: Analyze changes in log files.
diff.noteSecurity1: Pure Front-end Processing: Text comparison is done entirely in the browser — code, contracts and other sensitive content never leave the local machine.
diff.noteSecurity2: No Data Storage: No comparison history is saved — all data is cleared when you close the page.
diff.noteSecurity3: No Network Requests: The comparison process generates no network requests — works offline too.
diff.noteFile1: Only plain text files are supported; binary files are not.
diff.noteFile3: Large files may take longer to process, please be patient.
diff.notePerf1: Recommended to compare no more than 10,000 lines at a time. Diff computation for very large texts (tens of thousands of lines) may take longer and use more memory. For large file comparison, command-line tools (like Git diff or the diff command) are recommended.
diff.notePerf2: Comparison runs on the browser's main thread — the page may temporarily become unresponsive during computation. Large text comparisons auto-delay execution (using requestIdleCallback) to avoid blocking user interaction. Don't close the browser or refresh the page during processing.
diff.notePerf3: File upload only supports text files (UTF-8 encoded). Binary files (like .exe, .jpg, .pdf) cannot be correctly read as text for comparison. Uploading non-text files will show a 'file type not supported' message.
diff.noteEncoding2: Other encodings may cause garbled text; converting to UTF-8 before comparison is recommended.
diff.noteFaq1: Q: Too many differences to see clearly? A: Try checking 'Ignore whitespace' — many differences are actually just spaces and blank lines, ignoring them greatly reduces the diff volume.
diff.noteFaq2: Q: Can I compare two files? A: First copy the file contents into the input boxes. The current version doesn't support direct file upload for comparison.
diff.noteFaq3: Q: Can comparison results be exported? A: The current version doesn't support exporting as diff file format. You can take screenshots or use the browser's print-to-PDF function.
diff.noteFaq4: Performance issues: Reduce the text content or compare in smaller segments.

diff.problemsTitle: 1. Visual Comparison Is the Least Efficient Quality Control Method
diff.usagePasteText: Paste Text: Paste the "original version" and "modified version" text into the left and right input boxes respectively. Left = base text (old version), Right = comparison text (new version). The tool automatically analyzes the differences between them.
diff.usageUploadFile: Upload File: Click the "Upload File" button above each input box to select two text files. Supports .txt, .json, .csv, .html, .xml, .yaml and other common text formats. File content is automatically read and filled into the corresponding input box.
diff.usageClickCompare: Click Compare: Click "Start Compare" (or press Ctrl+Enter) to trigger the difference analysis. The algorithm compares the two texts line by line, finds the longest common subsequence (LCS), and marks lines not in the common sequence as added or deleted.
diff.usageViewResult: View Results: Results are displayed in a unified format below — green background lines indicate content added in the "modified version", red background lines indicate content deleted from the "original version". The top stats panel shows added, deleted, and unchanged line counts.
diff.usageTipSwap: Swap Text: Click the swap button between input boxes to quickly exchange the positions of left and right text — making the "modified version" the baseline and the "original version" the comparison target. The add/delete markers in the results will reverse accordingly.
diff.usageTipClear: Clear & Restart: Click "Clear" to remove all input and comparison results and start a new comparison task.
diff.noteAccuracy1: This tool uses line-by-line comparison strategy — splitting text into lines by newline characters, then comparing additions and deletions of lines. Character-level differences within a line are not independently highlighted. For finer-grained character-level comparison, use professional code review tools (like Git's word-diff mode).
diff.noteAccuracy2: The comparison algorithm is based on the Myers difference algorithm — finding the longest common subsequence (LCS) between two texts and marking lines not in the common sequence as differences. This algorithm produces results closest to human intuition, though multiple equivalent optimal solutions may exist.
diff.noteAccuracy3: Whitespace characters (spaces, tabs, blank lines) are considered valid content in the comparison. If the only differences between two texts are indentation or blank line count, these differences will also be marked. When comparing code, it's advisable to first unify indentation style (e.g., use 2-space or 4-space throughout).
diff.formatCode128: Line-Level Comparison: The algorithm splits both texts by lines and finds the longest common subsequence (LCS) — lines with the same sequence and identical content. Lines not in the common sequence are marked as differences: lines unique to the left are marked as "deleted", lines unique to the right as "added".
diff.formatEan13: Myers Algorithm: This tool uses Eugene Myers' O(ND) difference algorithm — time complexity is proportional to the amount of difference between the two texts, not the product of their lengths. This means comparing two 10,000-line files with only 50 different lines is very fast.
diff.formatUpc: Ignore Options: Check "Ignore Whitespace" to skip trailing spaces, consecutive spaces, and empty line differences — ideal for comparing code files (indentation style differences shouldn't count as differences). Check "Ignore Case" to treat Hello and hello as identical — suitable for case-insensitive content.

duplicate-finder.title: Duplicate Content Finder
duplicate-finder.intro: A duplicate content finder that automatically splits text by multiple separators, detects duplicate content, counts occurrences and highlights them in preview
duplicate-finder.inputPlaceholder:
Enter the text to check, supporting multiple separators such as spaces, commas and semicolons

e.g. [457,569,333,457,888,53,9,888]. Hello, hi, test, Hello
duplicate-finder.infoIntro: Duplicate Finder: Precisely Identify Duplicate Content with Hash Algorithms
duplicate-finder.problemTitle: 1. Why You Need a Duplicate Content Finder
duplicate-finder.problem1: Downloading the same attachment multiple times, different folders saving different copies of the same photo, backups without deduplication causing data to double — over time, duplicate files can occupy 20%-40% of storage space. Manual searching? File names may differ (e.g. report.pdf and report(1).pdf) but content is identical. This tool uses SHA-256 hash algorithm to calculate each file's 'digital fingerprint' — only files with identical content produce the same hash.
duplicate-finder.problem2: After uploading multiple files, the tool auto-calculates each file's SHA-256 hash, then groups by hash — files with the same hash are marked as duplicate groups. Shows the count of duplicates in each group, individual file size, and total wasted space. Supports one-click download of deduplicated file sets.
duplicate-finder.problem3: Pure front-end implementation — file hash calculation uses the Web Crypto API's SubtleCrypto interface, all computation done in the browser. Files are never uploaded to any server. Uses Web Workers for parallel hash calculation without blocking the main thread — the interface stays smooth even when processing large files.
duplicate-finder.formatText: Free Text: Supports text content separated by common separators like spaces, newlines, commas, semicolons, enumeration commas, pipes, etc. The system auto-identifies the separator used in the text and correctly splits entries. For example, 'apple, banana, apple, orange' is split into 4 entries, with 'apple' appearing 2 times.
duplicate-finder.formatCode: Code Data: Supports extracting values from code structures like arrays and lists — e.g. [457,569,333,457,888] auto-extracts numbers in brackets and checks for duplicates. Also supports structured data formats like JSON arrays, CSV column values.
duplicate-finder.featureOnline: Duplicate Groups: Files with identical content are grouped together — each group shows file count, individual file size, and wasted space ((count-1) x file size).
duplicate-finder.featurePreview: File Details: Each file shows file name, size, and hash value (first 16 characters). Convenient for confirming which files are duplicates.
duplicate-finder.featureExport: Deduplicated Download: Keeps one file from each duplicate group, marks the rest as deletable. Click 'Download Deduplicated Results' to batch download all unique files.
duplicate-finder.featureSecurity: Web Worker Parallel: Hash computation runs in a Web Worker — doesn't block the main thread, the interface stays responsive during processing. Multiple files can compute hashes in parallel.
duplicate-finder.usageInputContent: Enter content: Type the text you want to check for duplicates into the text box.
duplicate-finder.usageExampleFormat: Example formats: Multiple formats are supported, e.g. [457,569,333,457,888] or "Hello, hi, test, Hello".
duplicate-finder.usageSeparator: Separators: Multiple separators are detected automatically, including spaces, commas, semicolons and enumeration commas.
duplicate-finder.separatorCommon: Common separators: Space, comma (,), semicolon (;), enumeration comma (、), pipe (|), period (。), question mark (?), exclamation mark (!).
duplicate-finder.separatorSymbols: Symbols: Underscore (_), equals (=), plus (+), minus (-), asterisk (*), slash (/), backslash (\).

duplicate-finder.usageClick: Click Find Button: Click "Find Duplicates" (or press Ctrl+Enter) to start detection. Detection is extremely fast — even tens of thousands of items complete within milliseconds.
duplicate-finder.usageResultTags: Duplicate Tags: The results area displays all duplicate content as colored tags — each tag shows the duplicate text and its occurrence count (e.g., "Apple ×3"). Different duplicates use different colors for easy distinction.
duplicate-finder.usageResultFilter: Click to Filter: Click a duplicate tag to show only that duplicate's positions in the original preview — temporarily hiding other duplicates' highlighting. Click again to cancel filtering. Useful for locating specific content distribution among many duplicates.
duplicate-finder.usageResultPreview: Highlight Preview: All duplicate content in the original text is highlighted in corresponding colors — each duplicate uses a unique color so you can see at a glance which content appears multiple times. Non-duplicate content remains normally displayed.
duplicate-finder.noteAccuracy1: Duplicate detection is based on exact matching — two items must be completely identical (including case and spaces) to be flagged as duplicates. "Apple" and "apple" are treated as different items. For case-insensitive detection, convert the text to lowercase first.
duplicate-finder.noteAccuracy2: Empty items (empty strings) are excluded from detection. Consecutive separators (e.g., nothing between two commas) do not produce empty items. Leading and trailing spaces are automatically removed — " apple " and "apple" are treated as identical items.
duplicate-finder.noteAccuracy3: Separator detection is intelligent — the system analyzes the most commonly used separator in the text and prioritizes it. If multiple separators are used, all common separators are recognized. Brackets and parentheses are automatically stripped.
duplicate-finder.formatCode128: SHA-256 Hash: Maps files of any size to a fixed-length 256-bit (32-byte) digest. Theoretically different files could produce the same hash (collision), but SHA-256's collision probability is extremely low — roughly 2^128 files needed for a non-negligible chance, practically impossible in real-world use.
duplicate-finder.formatEan13: Content-Level Comparison: Unlike name/size-based deduplication, hash-based deduplication relies on file content — even if file names differ and save paths differ, as long as the content is identical, they are identified as duplicates. This is the most precise deduplication method.
duplicate-finder.formatUpc: Chunked Reading: Large files cannot be read into memory all at once — the tool uses FileReader's readAsArrayBuffer to read file content in chunks, then incrementally computes the hash using SubtleCrypto.digest. Even processing 1GB files does not cause memory overflow.
duplicate-finder.usageInput1: Batch Upload: Click or drag to upload multiple files. Supports any file format — the hash algorithm is format-independent.
duplicate-finder.usageInput2: File List: Uploaded files display as a list — file name, size, and status (computing/complete).
duplicate-finder.usageInput3: Large File Support: Supports processing large files (1GB+) — chunked reading prevents memory overflow. However, hash computation for large files takes longer.
duplicate-finder.usageFormat1: Automatic Start: Hash computation starts automatically after file upload — no need to manually click a "Start" button.
duplicate-finder.usageFormat2: Progress Display: Real-time computation progress — completed/total count.
duplicate-finder.usageFormat3: Parallel Computation: Multiple files compute hashes simultaneously — speed depends on CPU performance and file count.
duplicate-finder.usageFormat4: Completion Alert: After all files are computed, duplicate analysis runs automatically and results display.
duplicate-finder.usageFormat5: Result Grouping: Duplicate files display in groups — each group shows file count, size, and wasted space.
duplicate-finder.usageFormat6: No Duplicates: If all files have different content, displays a "No duplicate files found" message.
duplicate-finder.usageStyle1: Duplicate Group Details: Expand each duplicate group to see specific files — name, size, and hash.
duplicate-finder.usageStyle2: Waste Statistics: Top section shows overall stats — total files, duplicate files, total wasted space.
duplicate-finder.usageStyle3: Deduplication Suggestions: Each duplicate group recommends keeping one copy (typically the most standard file name) and deleting the rest.
duplicate-finder.usageGenerate1: Package Download: Click "Download Deduplicated Results" — keeping one copy per duplicate group, packaged as ZIP.
duplicate-finder.usageGenerate2: Manual Selection: If unsatisfied with auto-selection, manually check which files to keep in each group.
duplicate-finder.usageGenerate3: Cleanup Advice: After downloading deduplicated results, manually delete duplicate copies from the original files to free up storage space.
duplicate-finder.usageAdvice1: Retention Strategy: Keep the earliest created or most standard-named file per duplicate group — delete other copies.
duplicate-finder.usageAdvice2: Backup Scenarios: Run deduplication before backup — avoid copying duplicates to the backup drive, saving backup space and time.
duplicate-finder.usageAdvice3: Download Directories: Regularly clean duplicate files in download directories — downloading the same attachment multiple times is a major source of duplicates.
duplicate-finder.usageAdvice4: Photo Management: Photos exported from phones often have duplicates — different albums/export batches may contain the same photos.
duplicate-finder.noteFormat1: Browser Limitations: File upload is limited by browser memory and temporary storage — recommended total size per upload does not exceed 2GB.
duplicate-finder.noteFormat2: File Name Irrelevant: Deduplication is based on file content (hash value), independent of file names. Files with different names but identical content are still identified as duplicates.
duplicate-finder.noteFormat3: Directory Structure Not Preserved: Directory structure is not preserved during upload — all files are flattened. The deduplication download package also does not contain directory structure.
duplicate-finder.noteFormat4: Empty File Handling: Empty files (0 bytes) have identical hash values and are grouped together as duplicates. This is generally expected behavior.

num-to-chinese.title: Number to Chinese Converter
num-to-chinese.intro: Number-to-Chinese tool that converts Arabic numerals to Chinese uppercase amounts and vice versa, supporting decimals and negative numbers. Ideal for finance, contracts and other scenarios
num-to-chinese.num2cnHint: Supports up to 16 integer digits (about 9999 trillion), with a maximum of two decimal places
num-to-chinese.num2cnNote: Note: Supports integer and decimal conversion, up to the trillion digit, keeping at most two decimal places. Negative numbers are converted to Chinese uppercase with a leading "negative". "Yuan" is added before the decimal point, and the decimal parts use "jiao" and "fen".
num-to-chinese.cn2numNote: Note: Converts Chinese uppercase numerals to Arabic numerals. "元", "圆" and "点" are unified into decimal points, and quantifiers such as "角" and "分" are automatically parsed as decimal places. The result keeps two decimal places.
num-to-chinese.infoIntro: Number to Chinese: Precisely Convert Arabic Numerals to Chinese Uppercase/Lowercase Amounts
num-to-chinese.problemsTitle: 1. Why Financial Systems Need 'Number to Chinese'
num-to-chinese.problem1: The amount on a bank check must use Chinese uppercase (壹万式仟参佰肆拾伍元陆角柒分) — this is to prevent tampering: the Arabic numeral '10000' can be easily changed to '90000', but changing '壹万' to '玖万' requires altering the entire character, immediately obvious. This isn't just format conversion, it's a financial security necessity. This tool supports converting any number to Chinese uppercase amount, lowercase amount, and Chinese reading format.
num-to-chinese.problem2: The Chinese number system has two 'counting methods': the reading system (一、十、百、千、万、亿) for daily reading, like '一千二百三十四'; the financial system (壹、贰、参、拾、佰、仟、萬、億) for tickets and contracts, preventing alteration. This tool supports both systems and auto-handles the 'zero' insertion rules (e.g. 1001 → 壹仟零壹元整, not 壹仟壹元整).
num-to-chinese.problem3: Supports integers, decimals and negative numbers. The decimal part auto-identifies as jiao/fen (amount mode) or reads digit by digit (reading mode). Precision supports up to fen (two decimal places) — meeting the vast majority of financial scenarios. Pure front-end calculation, no data uploaded.
num-to-chinese.formatNumber: Arabic Numbers: Supports integers up to 16 digits (approximately 9999 trillion) and up to two decimal places. Negative numbers are supported. The tool automatically handles the insertion rules for "零" (zero) — e.g., 1001 → "壹仟零壹元整," not "壹仟壹元整."
num-to-chinese.formatChinese: Chinese Numerals: Supports both simplified (一二三) and traditional financial numerals (壹贰叁). Input can include "元"/"圆"/"点" as decimal point markers, and "角"/"分" as decimal place values. The result is rounded to two decimal places.
num-to-chinese.featureOnline: Zero Handling: Consecutive zeros read as one '零' — e.g. 10001 → '壹万零壹元整' (not '壹万零零零壹元整'). Zeros at the end of a unit are not read — e.g. 12000 → '壹万贰仟元整'.
num-to-chinese.featurePreview: Jiao Handling: When there's jiao but no fen, '整' is not added at the end — e.g. 1.50 → '壹元伍角'. When there's neither jiao nor fen, '整' is added — e.g. 1.00 → '壹元整'. When there's both jiao and fen, '整' is also not added — e.g. 1.56 → '壹元伍角陆分'.
num-to-chinese.featureExport: Negative Number Support: Negative numbers add '负' at the front — e.g. -100 → '负壹佰元整'. Suitable for representing refunds, losses, etc.
num-to-chinese.featureSecurity: Precision Control: Amount mode supports up to two decimal places (jiao/fen). More than two decimal places are rounded to fen — this is standard practice for financial systems.

num-to-chinese.formatLower: Lowercase Chinese Numerals: Uses "零一二三四五六七八九" with "十百千万亿". Suitable for everyday text — e.g., "Page three hundred twenty-five", "Q2", "Five hundred million population". This is the most common Chinese numeral representation.
num-to-chinese.formatUpper: Uppercase Chinese Numerals: Uses "零壹贰叁肆伍陆柒捌玖" with "拾佰仟万亿". Exclusively for financial documents and formal files — the complex strokes make alteration difficult, providing tamper-proof functionality. For example, bank check amounts must use uppercase: "人民币壹万贰仟叁佰肆拾伍元整".
num-to-chinese.usageInputContent: Enter Value: Type the number to convert in the input box. Supports positive integers (e.g., 12345), decimals (e.g., 123.45), and negative numbers (e.g., -12345). Number range supports from trillions (10^12) down to two decimal places.
num-to-chinese.usageInputRange: Value Range: Maximum supported value is ±9999,9999,9999,9999.99 (approx. 10^16). Numbers beyond this range may not convert correctly. For very large amounts, process in segments.
num-to-chinese.usageResultLower: Lowercase Chinese: Displays standard lowercase Chinese numerals — e.g., 12345 → "一万二千三百四十五". Suitable for everyday text and general number representation.
num-to-chinese.usageResultUpper: Uppercase Chinese: Displays finance-specific uppercase Chinese numerals — e.g., 12345 → "壹万贰仟叁佰肆拾伍". Suitable for checks, invoices, contracts and other formal documents.
num-to-chinese.usageResultMoney: Standard Amount Format: Displays the complete financial amount format — e.g., 12345.67 → "壹万贰仟叁佰肆拾伍元陆角柒分". Integer amounts automatically add "整" (e.g., "壹万元整").
num-to-chinese.usageCopy: One-Click Copy: Each format has a copy button — click to copy the corresponding Chinese numeral to the clipboard. Paste directly into Word documents, Excel spreadsheets, or financial software.
num-to-chinese.noteAccuracy1: The rule for using "零" in Chinese numerals is complex — consecutive zeros are read as only one "零" (e.g., 1001 → "一千零一", not "一千零零一"), zeros at the beginning of a wan section need to be read (e.g., 1,0001 → "一万零一"), trailing zeros are not read (e.g., 1000 → "一千", not "一千零零零"). This tool strictly follows these rules.
num-to-chinese.noteAccuracy2: In uppercase amounts, after "元", if there are no jiao 角 or fen 分, add "整" (e.g., "壹佰元整"). If there are jiao but no fen, "整" may be omitted (e.g., "壹佰元伍角"). If there are fen, "整" is not added (e.g., "壹佰元伍角陆分"). The tool automatically handles these rules.
num-to-chinese.noteAccuracy3: The number "2" has two representations in Chinese — "二" (lowercase) and "两" (colloquial). This tool uniformly uses "二" (lowercase mode) and "贰" (uppercase mode). In speech, "200" is often said as "两百" rather than "二百", but both are acceptable in writing.
num-to-chinese.formatCode128: Upper Amount: Finance-specific format using uppercase characters 壹贰叁肆伍陆柒捌玖拾佰仟萬億. Output format like "人民币壹万贰仟叁佰肆拾伍元陆角柒分". Automatically adds the "人民币" prefix and "整" suffix (added when no jiao/fen, omitted when jiao/fen present).
num-to-chinese.formatEan13: Lowercase Amount: Uses regular numerals — 一, 二, 三, 十, 百, 千, 万, 亿. Output format like "一万二千三百四十五元六角七分". Suitable for informal Chinese texts requiring Chinese amounts.
num-to-chinese.formatUpc: Chinese Reading: Reads digits one by one — e.g., 12345 → "一二三四五". Suitable for phone numbers, room numbers, IDs and other scenarios that don't require place-value reading.
num-to-chinese.usageInput1: Enter Number: Type an Arabic numeral in the input box — supports integers and decimals. E.g., 12345.67.

qrcode.problem1: How much information can a 30x30 pixel black-and-white block store? The answer is 174 numeric characters or 98 alphabetic characters — that's the capacity of QR Code standard version 3. QR codes use four encoding modes (numeric, alphanumeric, byte, kanji) to auto-select the most compact representation. Even more remarkably, even if 30% of the area is obscured, the QR code can still be correctly read — thanks to the Reed-Solomon error correction algorithm.
qrcode.problem2: This tool generates standard QR codes based on the qrcode-generator library — supports four error correction levels (L/M/Q/H), customizable size, foreground/background color customization. timestamp.problem1: Unix timestamp — the number of seconds (or milliseconds) from 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC to now. Databases store 1693814400, APIs return 1693814400000, log files write 1693814400 — but humans need to see '2023-09-04 16:00:00'. Converting between timestamps and readable dates is a daily high-frequency operation for developers, ops engineers, and data analysts.

timestamp.usageFormat3: Dual Format Output: Displays both second-level (10-digit) and millisecond-level (13-digit) timestamps — choose based on your use case.
timestamp.usageFormat4: Current Time: Real-time display of current timestamp and date — auto-updates every second for quick reference.
timestamp.usageFormat5: Copy Function: Click the copy button next to a timestamp or date — convenient for pasting into code or logs.
timestamp.usageFormat6: Clear & Retry: Auto-recalculates when input changes — no need to manually click any button.
timestamp.usageStyle1: On the Hour: Second-level timestamps at each hour are multiples of 3600 — e.g., 2023-09-04 16:00:00 UTC = 1693843200.
timestamp.usageStyle2: Day Boundary: The timestamp for 00:00:00 each day = multiples of 86400 — convenient for grouping data by day.
timestamp.usageStyle3: Timezone Offset: Beijing Time = UTC + 8 hours = UTC + 28800 seconds — timestamps themselves don't contain timezone info; timezone is applied when displaying.
timestamp.usageAdvice1: Store in UTC: Always store UTC timestamps in the database — convert to user timezone on display. Avoid daylight saving time and timezone confusion.
timestamp.usageAdvice2: Seconds vs Milliseconds: Pay attention to distinguishing 10-digit (seconds) and 13-digit (milliseconds) timestamps — mixing them up will show dates from 1970 or the distant future.
timestamp.usageAdvice3: Timezone Annotation: API-returned timestamps should clearly indicate the timezone (usually UTC) — preventing client-side misinterpretation.
timestamp.usageAdvice4: Overflow Protection: When processing user-input timestamps, check for reasonable ranges — negative timestamps indicate pre-1970 dates, excessively large values may be milliseconds mistaken for seconds.
timestamp.noteFormat1: UTC: Coordinated Universal Time — the global time standard, unaffected by daylight saving. Servers and APIs typically use UTC.
timestamp.noteFormat2: Daylight Saving Time: Some timezones observe DST (e.g., US, Europe) — clocks advance 1 hour in summer. This tool automatically handles DST offsets.
timestamp.noteFormat3: Timezone Database: Timezone rules may change due to policy updates — this tool uses the browser's built-in timezone data, staying synchronized with the operating system.
timestamp.noteFormat4: Timestamp Essence: Unix timestamps are absolute (the same moment globally has the same timestamp value); local time is relative (different timezones show different values).

json.title: JSON Toolkit
json.desc: JSON toolkit with formatting, comparison, Java Bean conversion, XML conversion, compression, and more. Supports node folding and diff highlighting with syntax validation.

intro.title: Tool Introduction
intro.aboutTitle: 1. Why You Need a Professional JSON Tool
intro.about1: Every backend developer has experienced this: copying an API response from logs, pasting it into an editor, and finding it's a compressed one-liner — thousands of key-value pairs crammed together, braces and brackets nested layers deep, impossible to find the target field by eye. It gets worse when you need to compare configuration differences between environments or convert JSON received by the frontend into Java entity classes — manual operations are both inefficient and error-prone.
intro.about2: This tool was designed to solve these everyday pain points. It's not a simple "formatter" — it's a comprehensive JSON lifecycle workstation: from reading (formatting + folding + searching), to analysis (dual-pane diff comparison), to conversion (generating Java Beans, converting to XML) — all operations switch seamlessly within a single page, no need to jump between multiple tools.
intro.about3: A note on security: this tool is a pure frontend application — it doesn't rely on any backend APIs or send your data to any server. API keys, database configurations, and user information you paste into the editor exist only in your browser's memory. Closing the tab clears everything completely; even incognito mode leaves no traces.
intro.module1: The Formatting Module goes far beyond "adding indentation." It has a built-in fault-tolerant parser: strips UTF-8 BOM (Windows Notepad's "handiwork"), removes JSONC comments (VS Code's settings.json style), corrects single quotes to double quotes, supports Python-style True/False/None, and tolerates trailing commas. These "non-standard but common" patterns would cause errors in other tools but are intelligently corrected here. The formatted editor is based on CodeMirror 6, supporting syntax highlighting, line numbers, fuzzy search, and node folding — quickly locating target fields even in large files.
intro.module2: The Comparison Module uses a line-by-line diff algorithm, but it's not simple text comparison — it first standardizes both JSON segments (ignoring whitespace and field order), then precisely marks "which element in which array changed" or "which property of which object was modified." Added, deleted, and modified differences are highlighted in different colors. Synchronized formatting/compression/escape buttons ensure both sides are always in the same processing state, avoiding "false differences" caused by inconsistent formatting.
intro.module3: The Java Bean Conversion Module addresses a frequent need: quickly generating corresponding Java entity classes from a JSON response. It doesn't just map field names and types — every field in the generated code is automatically filled with the actual JSON value as an initialization example (private String name = "John";), making it easy to understand field meanings. Type inference covers String, Long, Double, Boolean, List, nested objects, and more. Reverse conversion is also supported — generating JSON templates from Java Bean code.
intro.module4: The XML Conversion Module handles mapping between two data formats. When converting JSON to XML, nested objects become child elements, array elements become repeating tags, with attribute mode support; when converting XML to JSON, element names become key names, attributes are identified with a $ prefix, text is stored with _text, and duplicate named elements are automatically merged into arrays. Results are auto-formatted, ready for SOAP interface debugging, configuration file migration, and more.
intro.feature1: Smart Fault Tolerance: Automatically removes BOM and comments, converts single quotes to double quotes, supports Python-style True/False/None, tolerates trailing commas.
intro.feature2: Fuzzy Key-Value Search: Fuzzy matching on keys and values, results show line numbers and full paths, click to jump to location.
intro.feature3: Escape State Recognition: Clicking format while escaped automatically un-escapes first; display state is restored after un-escaping.
intro.feature4: Modern Editor: Based on CodeMirror 6, supporting syntax highlighting, line numbers, word wrap, fullscreen, and dark mode.

format.title: 1. Formatting: From Chaos to Clarity
format.item1: Paste compressed JSON into the editor and click "Format." The fault-tolerant engine automatically fixes common issues (BOM, comments, single quotes, trailing commas), outputting a readable format with indentation and syntax highlighting. If the JSON has syntax errors (e.g., mismatched brackets), the editor shows a red marker and specific error description at the error position, precise to line and column number.
format.item2: The "Minify" button performs the inverse of formatting — removes all whitespace and line breaks, compressing JSON to a single line. Comments are automatically stripped before minification. This is useful when you need to reduce JSON size (storing in databases, transmitting over networks). Escaped content can also be minified directly; the tool processes escaping first.
format.item3: The "Escape" button converts special characters in JSON to escape sequences (newline→\n, quote→\", backslash→\\), commonly used for embedding JSON in JavaScript strings or log output. "Un-escape" does the reverse. The tool remembers the pre-escape state (formatted or minified) and restores it after un-escaping.
format.item4: The "Collapse" button collapses all nested nodes at once — objects show {5 properties}, arrays show [3 elements], making it easy to browse the top-level structure of large JSON. Click again to expand all nodes. Collapsing depends on formatted structural information; if not formatted, it prompts "Please format first."
format.item5: The "Search" button opens a search panel supporting fuzzy matching on key names and values (case-insensitive). Each search result shows match type, line number, and full JSON path (e.g., data.users[0].address.city), clicking a result auto-scrolls and highlights the selection. Search doesn't require prior formatting — as long as the content is parseable as JSON.
format.item6: The "New Line" button displays single-line JSON with structural line breaks (one key-value pair per line) without changing semantics — between formatting and minifying, suitable for viewing embedded long strings (like Base64 data, HTML fragments).
format.item7: The bottom of the editor provides the same button group as the top — no need to scroll back up when working with long documents. The "Example" button loads a sample JSON containing various data types for quickly exploring features.

compare.title: 2. Comparison: Precisely Locate Every Difference
compare.item1: Switch to the "Compare" tab, paste the JSON data to compare on the left and right sides. After clicking "Start Compare," the system performs structural diff analysis on both JSON segments — additions highlighted in green, deletions in red, modifications in yellow. For arrays, it pinpoints exactly which element changed; for objects, it identifies which specific property was modified.
compare.item2: Four sync buttons (format/minify/escape/clear) act on both sides simultaneously. It's recommended to click "Sync Format" first to ensure both sides have consistent formatting before comparing — otherwise indentation differences will be misidentified as content differences. The comparison algorithm ignores object field order differences ({"a":1,"b":2} and {"b":2,"a":1} are treated as identical), but array element order differences are flagged.
compare.item3: If both JSON segments are identical, the comparison result area displays "The two JSON inputs are identical." For large JSON (over 3000 lines), comparison may take 2-3 seconds — please be patient.

javabean.title: 3. JSON ↔ Java Bean Bidirectional Conversion
javabean.item1: In the "To Java" tab, paste JSON on the left side and click "To Bean." The tool traverses the JSON structure, generating a Java class for each object: the object name is taken from the key name (first letter capitalized), and field types are automatically inferred from values (string→String, integer→Long, decimal→Double, boolean→Boolean, array→List, nested object→separate class). Each field is automatically filled with the actual JSON value as an initialization example.
javabean.item2: Type inference strategy: integers are preferentially inferred as Long (not int) to avoid large number overflow; decimals are inferred as Double; null values are inferred as Object and need manual adjustment. If fields differ across elements in the same array, the tool uses the first element as the basis for type inference.
javabean.item3: Reverse conversion is also supported — paste Java Bean code on the right side and click "To JSON." The tool parses field declarations and type annotations to generate corresponding JSON templates. Field initial values are extracted as sample data in the JSON.
javabean.item4: Generated Java code can be copied directly into an IDE. If class or field names conflict with Java keywords, the tool automatically adds prefixes to avoid compilation errors.

xml.title: 4. JSON ↔ XML Bidirectional Conversion
xml.item1: In the "To XML" tab, paste JSON on the left side and click "To XML." Conversion rules: JSON object keys become XML element names, string/number values become element text, nested objects become child elements, and array elements become repeating tags with the same name. Results are automatically indented and formatted.
xml.item2: During reverse conversion (XML→JSON), XML element names become JSON key names, element attributes are identified with a $ prefix (e.g., $id), and text content is stored with the _text key. Multiple elements with the same name are automatically merged into a JSON array. The root element serves as the outermost wrapper.
xml.item3: Both format conversions preserve complete hierarchical structure and data content. Results can be directly used for SOAP interface debugging, configuration file format migration, data import/export, and other scenarios.

security.title: 1. Facts About Data Security
security.item1: This tool is a pure frontend application — the entire code runs in your browser with no backend server. Your JSON data (including API keys, database passwords, user information, etc.) is never sent through any network request. You can verify with your browser's developer tools (F12 → Network): after opening the tool, besides the page's own load requests, no additional network communication is generated.
security.item2: Nevertheless, processing highly sensitive data on public computers (internet cafes, libraries) is not recommended. The reason isn't that data gets uploaded — it's that browser memory and system clipboard can be read by other programs on the same machine. If using a public device, please clear the editor, clear the clipboard, and close the tab when finished.
security.item3: After processing sensitive data, click the "Clear" button to clear the editor content. Although the browser automatically releases memory after closing the tab, proactive clearing is a safer habit. For JSON containing keys, it's recommended to additionally clear the browser clipboard (paste blank content once to overwrite).

format.title: 2. Format Compatibility and Fault Tolerance Boundaries
format.item1: The standard JSON specification (RFC 8259) requires: key names and strings must use double quotes, no comments allowed, no trailing commas, no support for undefined or functions. But real-world JSON data is often "not quite standard" — from JavaScript config files, Python script output, or manually edited content. This tool's fault-tolerant engine covers the following common "non-standard" cases:
format.item2: Single-quoted strings: automatically corrects 'value' to "value". However, if the string content itself contains unescaped single quotes (like 'it's fine'), auto-correction may produce incorrect results — manual correction before formatting is recommended.
format.item3: Trailing commas: the last comma in {"a":1,"b":2,} is automatically removed. JavaScript's JSON.parse doesn't tolerate this, but many editors (VS Code) and language JSON libraries (Python, Java) support it.
format.item4: JSONC comments: // single-line comments and /* multi-line comments */ are automatically stripped during formatting. If you need to preserve comments, back up the original content before formatting. Note: VS Code's settings.json, tsconfig.json, and similar files use JSONC format — comments will be lost after formatting.

usage.title: 3. Usage Tips and Common Misconceptions
usage.item1: The folding feature depends on formatted structural information. Unformatted JSON is a single line of plain text; the tool can't identify node boundaries, so the collapse button prompts "Please format first." After formatting, each object and array can be independently folded — folded objects show property count, arrays show element count, making it easy to browse the top-level structure of large JSON.
usage.item2: Search doesn't require prior formatting — it performs regex matching directly on the original text. But formatted search results are more intuitive (with line numbers, collapsible positioning). The search panel supports matching key names and values separately, showing full JSON paths (e.g., data.users[2].email), clicking a result auto-scrolls to the corresponding position.
usage.item3: The comparison feature standardizes JSON before comparing — ignoring whitespace differences and object field order. But array element order differences are flagged — [1,2,3] and [3,2,1] are treated as different. If you only care about content, not order, sort arrays before comparing.
usage.item4: The escape feature is commonly used to embed JSON in other formats (like JavaScript strings, SQL statements, log output). Escaped JSON looks like gibberish with backslashes — this is normal. It's still valid JSON, just with all special characters escaped. Un-escaping restores the original readable format.

performance.title: 4. Large File Processing Recommendations
performance.item1: When processing JSON files over 10MB, the formatting operation needs to build a complete syntax tree and render it in the CodeMirror editor, which may cause the browser to freeze for several seconds. CodeMirror's syntax highlighting also consumes significant CPU on large files. It's recommended to process large JSON in segments — extract sub-structures of interest for formatting analysis rather than loading the entire file at once.
performance.item2: Deeply nested JSON (over 10 levels) may have brief delays during fold/expand operations due to recursive DOM node traversal. Search performance also degrades on large files (over 1MB). The tool uses requestIdleCallback optimization to avoid blocking user interaction, but large file operations still require patience.
performance.item3: The comparison feature has O(N×M) time complexity, where N and M are the line counts of both JSON segments. Comparing two 5000-line JSON files may take 2-3 seconds. If comparing large configuration files, consider minifying first then comparing key differences.

compatibility.title: 5. Browser and Encoding
compatibility.item1: Recommended: Chrome 80+, Firefox 75+, Edge 80+, Safari 13+. The CodeMirror 6 editor depends on ES6+ features (Proxy, Symbol) and doesn't support IE 11. Chrome/Edge's JavaScript engine offers the best performance for large file processing. Mobile browsers can open the tool for basic operations, but the editing experience isn't as good as desktop.
compatibility.item2: Ensure input data uses UTF-8 encoding. Content copied from Windows Notepad may be GBK encoded — Chinese characters will appear garbled. Copying from web pages/PDFs may introduce invisible characters (zero-width spaces, BOM markers); the fault-tolerant engine automatically removes BOM, but other invisible characters need manual cleanup.
compatibility.item3: The escape feature handles special characters (newline→\n, quote→\", etc.). Chinese characters and emoji are preserved as Unicode by default, without \uXXXX escaping, ensuring the escaped JSON remains readable.

encoding.title: 6. Common JSON Questions
encoding.item1: Why does my JSON formatting fail? Most common reasons: 1) Key names not wrapped in double quotes (JSON doesn't allow single-quoted or unquoted key names); 2) Trailing commas (tolerated by some languages but not standard JSON); 3) Mismatched brackets (brace and bracket counts don't match). The fault-tolerant engine automatically attempts corrections, but severe errors require manual fixing.
encoding.item2: Why don't the comparison results match what I see? The tool standardizes JSON before comparing (ignoring whitespace and field order), so {"a":1,"b":2} and {"b":2,"a":1} are treated as identical. If you do see differences, they represent content-level differences rather than formatting differences.
encoding.item3: Do Java Bean conversion results need manual adjustment? In most cases, the generated code can be used directly. But these situations require manual modification: 1) Different elements in the same array have different fields — the tool uses the first element as the standard; 2) null values are inferred as Object type; 3) integers are inferred as Long instead of Integer. It's recommended to review in an IDE after generation.

faq.title: 7. Troubleshooting Guide
faq.item1: Content lost after formatting? Check if the original JSON has duplicate key names — JSON standard allows duplicate keys (later ones override earlier ones), and formatting automatically deduplicates. If the original data relies on duplicate keys to convey different information, you'll need to use array structures instead.
faq.item2: Search can't find content that clearly exists? Search is regex-based; if your search term contains regex special characters (like ., *, [), they need to be escaped with backslashes. Also, search distinguishes between Unicode encoding and original characters — if Chinese in JSON is \uXXXX encoded, searching for the original Chinese characters won't find matches.
faq.item3: Strange $ and _text in XML conversion results? This is the XML attribute to JSON key mapping convention. XML attributes have no corresponding JSON concept, so the tool uses $attributeName prefix to distinguish attributes from child elements; when text content and child elements coexist, text is stored with the _text key. This is the industry-standard XML→JSON mapping rule.
